Effect: From the start of each round after the first, one player rolls a d6: 1-4 no rain yet, 5+ the rain begins (no more rolls). Once raining: fighters see only 12"; subtract 1 from misfire rolls (min 1).

A tower terrain feature is placed at the centre. A warband with a Leader or Champion wholly within 6" horizontally of the centre automatically passes flee tests. Hold the Centre scores 3 VP instead of d3.
Aftermath / Campaign Effect: The winner gains 1 exploration re-roll in the aftermath sequence

Effect: Both warbands use 3 battle groups instead of 2.
Reinforcements start in round 6 instead of 3.

At the start of every round, the warband with fewer VP picks 1 enemy fighter on the battlefield to be condemned until the end of the round. Taking down a condemned fighter scores the opposing warband 1 extra VP.

The underdog places a chest on the floor wholly within 6" of one of the entry points that no player picked (token or terrain). A Leader or Champion within 3" of the chest automatically passes flee tests. At the end of each round, a warband with fighters within 3" of the chest and no enemy fighters within 3" scores 1 extra VP.
Aftermath / Campaign Effect: The winner claims the chest and rolls on the Chest table (see scenario_tables.csv)

Effect: At the end of a fighter's activation, if holding treasure they must pass a Willpower test or suffer d3 damage (no drop check for that damage). Demon and Undead fighters are unaffected.
Treasure tokens are placed alternately until there are 5 instead of 3. The first time a fighter moves within 3" of a token, roll a d6: on 1-2 it is worthless and removed.
Fighters see only 9".
Add 1 to melee attack rolls for fighters not holding treasure that are engaged in melee with an enemy fighter that is holding treasure.

Instead of 3 tokens, only 1 is placed by the underdog within 3" of the centre. When a token is picked up for the first time, another is placed scattered 3d6" from the centre. This repeats; at most 5 tokens in total.
A wagon is placed at the centre if the players have a suitable model. Instead of 3 tokens, the underdog places 6, each within 3" of the centre and more than 1" from the others.

At the start of each round roll a d6 for each quarter: on 4+ it is masked in fog. Fighters are not visible to each other beyond 6" if at least one is in a masked quarter. If no quarters are masked after rolling, the fog lifts and no more rolls are made.
Ignore battle groups and reinforcements. Each player sets up their whole warband wholly within 9" horizontally of their entry point.
From round 4, at the start of the round, a player with fewer domination marks can pick a quarter to be the forsaken quarter for that round. It cannot be controlled.
The quarter containing a warband's entry point is its home quarter. A player scores 3 marks instead of 1 for controlling the opposing warband's home quarter.
From round 3, at the start of each round the players randomly choose a critical quarter. A player scores 1 additional mark for controlling it.
A statue is placed at the centre. A fighter that finishes its activation within 6" of the centre heals d3 life. Demon and Undead fighters are unaffected.
The underdog places 5 treasure tokens inside the chapel instead of 3: one within 1" of each corner and one at the centre.

The first time a fighter is taken down within the chapel, a player rolls on the Desecrated Ground table (see scenario_tables.csv). The table is rolled again each time a Thunder Claps result comes up and a fighter is next taken down in the chapel.

A stone sarcophagus is placed at the centre. A fighter touching it and not engaged in melee can try to pry off the lid as an action: roll a d6, 1-5 fails, 6+ succeeds, +1 for each previous attempt by a friendly fighter in the same round. Beasts cannot try. If the battle ends before the lid is pried off, the winner pries it off automatically with a friendly fighter that was not taken down (no roll), and all such friendly fighters count as in the chapel while no enemy fighters do. When the lid comes off, roll on the Sarcophagus table (see scenario_tables.csv).
Aftermath / Campaign Effect: The prying fighter earns +2d6 bonus XP; results on the Sarcophagus table can give a treasure token worth 3d6x5 silver or a relic roll

Effect: The Hit starts drunk. Each time it is picked to activate, roll a d6: 1-5 it scatters d6" and its activation ends; 6 it sobers up. It also sobers up as soon as it suffers damage or is engaged in melee. Demon and Undead fighters ignore this.
Fighters see only 9" and misfire rolls get -1 (min 1). From round 2, roll a d6 at the start of each round; if the result is less than the round number the downpour ends.
Add 3 to the Hit's Life value for this battle.

The Defender places 2 tokens on the floor within 6" of each other and off the street. If the Hit finishes a move within 1/2" of one and is not engaged in melee, it can move through to the other token (it may be set up in melee); then remove both tokens.
During deployment the Ambusher can set up fighters within 12" of enemy fighters if those fighters are at least 3" vertically above the floor and more than 9" from all enemy fighters.
Both of the Defender's battle groups arrive at the start of round 3.

A fire in the holding smoulders at first (no effect). At the start of each round roll a d6: on 4+ it becomes a blaze; later on another 4+ it becomes an inferno (no more rolls). Blaze: a fighter that finishes a move having passed within the holding suffers d3 damage. Inferno: also, at the end of each round roll a d6 for each treasure token in the holding; on 4+ it is destroyed.
The Defender's warband does not take flee tests.
Keep 3 wall pieces (each no longer than 5") aside. When the Defender deploys, they roll a d3 and place that many wall sections on the edge of the holding.
Reinforcements start in round 6 instead of 3.
During deployment the Attacker can set up fighters from both battle groups anywhere wholly within 6" horizontally of a battlefield edge. The Defender's fighters can pick up treasure from round 1.
8 treasure tokens are placed within 3" of the centre of the holding instead of 5.
